title: AI Campaign Production
description: A lightweight control layer for AI-assisted campaign assembly across Jira, CMS and DAM, with human attention focused on exceptions and consequential decisions.
reviewQuestions: Does the Attention → Campaigns → Actions / Manifest model make the workflow legible without recreating CMS or DAM?
Are intervention states and automated readiness states visually distinct enough?
Can reviewers understand what automation assembled, what still needs a human, and where to go next?

revisions.name: v1 · Stable V0 handoff
revisions.summary: Established the accepted information architecture: global Attention and Campaigns, with campaign-level Actions and Manifest, plus the stable master-detail shell.
revisions.scope: Accepted V0 baseline. This revision is the protected starting point for the Cursor hardening pass.
preserve: Attention and Campaigns remain the two top-level views.
A selected campaign uses Actions and Manifest only.
The master-detail shell and status-first campaign list remain intact.
CMS and DAM remain systems of record rather than being recreated in Campaign Production.
acceptanceChecks: Accepted shell, Campaigns table and split-view interaction render without layout regressions.
Attention and campaign Actions continue to represent the same underlying unresolved work.
Actions and Manifest remain the selected-campaign information architecture.

workingMode.requestedAmendment: Harden the accepted v1 prototype in Cursor through small, controlled implementation changes rather than broad regeneration.
mayChange: Semantic Status message treatment in Attention, Actions and Manifest.
CMS/DAM action semantics and simulated external-resolution behaviour.
Reset behaviour, accessibility and regression coverage.
mustRemainUnchanged: The accepted Attention / Campaigns and Actions / Manifest information architecture.
The stable master-detail shell and status-first campaign list.
CMS and DAM as systems of record.
Shared state between global Attention and campaign Actions.
acceptanceChecks: Previously accepted screens remain visually and behaviourally intact outside the requested amendment.
Autumn Trail action resolution, Black Friday review failure, Winter Running sign-off, Archive, Duplicate and Reset all complete without stale state.
Campaign Production remains a lightweight control layer rather than expanding into CMS/DAM editing.

decisionLog.decision: Use Attention and Campaigns as the two top-level views, with Actions and Manifest inside a selected campaign.
decisionLog.rationale: This separates operational follow-up from campaign status and avoids rebuilding CMS/DAM navigation inside the control layer.

decisionLog.decision: Treat CMS and DAM as systems of record.
decisionLog.rationale: Campaign Production should explain state, surface exceptions and route the user to detailed production work rather than duplicate existing editing surfaces.

decisionLog.decision: Protect the accepted baseline during sequential iteration.
decisionLog.rationale: The V0 phase showed that broad rewrites could regress already accepted screens. A candidate revision must build from the accepted revision and promotion must be explicit.

decisionLog.decision: Do not use Overview / Content / Assets as campaign tabs.
decisionLog.rationale: That structure made the control layer feel like another CMS/DAM browser rather than a workflow-oriented production surface.

context.problem: Campaign production spans source tickets, structured CMS content and DAM assets. Mechanical assembly can be automated, but users still need a clear view of progress, exceptions and consequential decisions.
context.intendedOutcome: Produce a credible first draft of a campaign automatically while keeping human attention focused on unresolved or uncertain work and preserving direct paths into the systems of record.
context.workflow: A source ticket triggers campaign interpretation, asset and content discovery, CMS/DAM assembly and readiness checks. Campaign Production then surfaces unresolved actions and a read-only manifest of what was assembled.
context.currentDirection: A restrained enterprise control layer: Attention shows cross-campaign work that needs a human; Campaigns shows status; Actions shows what must happen next; Manifest shows what automation created and where it lives.
constraints: Do not become another CMS or DAM.
Do not hide consequential automation or unresolved exceptions.
Use shared underlying state for global Attention and campaign Actions.
Preserve accepted screens when making a sequential amendment.
Keep detailed content and asset editing in the systems of record.
acceptedDecisions: Attention and Campaigns are the top-level information architecture.
Actions and Manifest are the selected-campaign views.
Folders appear before Content and Assets in Manifest.
Campaign lifecycle status is distinct from object readiness status.
Signed-off campaigns can be duplicated; all non-archived campaigns can be archived.
openQuestions: What is the clearest final treatment for semantic status messages in Attention, Actions and Manifest?
How should external CMS/DAM state changes be simulated in the portfolio prototype without implying false integration?
Which future questions genuinely require divergent exploration rather than another sequential revision?

title: Needs Remediation
description: Reference project showing how a divergent exploration set can branch from an accepted revision, select a direction, and then promote that direction into a later accepted revision.
reviewQuestions: Does the selected direction distinguish a fixed saved-view definition from user-controlled narrowing filters?
Does the task-first toolbar preserve the production table while making the operational goal clearer?

revisions.name: v1 · Production baseline
revisions.summary: Captured the trusted production starting point before changing the filter/header model.
revisions.scope: No redesign. Preserve the existing product surface as the accepted baseline for the exploration.
preserve: Existing message table structure and row behaviour.
Bulk actions and established operational workflow.
acceptanceChecks: Production table structure remains represented accurately.
The baseline is retained for comparison with later alternatives.

revisions.name: v2 · Task-first HiFi
revisions.summary: Integrated the selected task-first direction into a high-fidelity revision while preserving the trusted message table.
revisions.scope: Refine the header and filter model so the operational task and fixed saved-view definition are clearer.
preserve: Existing message table structure and row behaviour.
One stable name for the Needs Remediation view.
The distinction between fixed view definition and user-controlled filters.
acceptanceChecks: The fixed view definition no longer reads like removable filters.
The operational task is more prominent.
The underlying message table remains unchanged.

explorationSets.name: Filter/header directions
explorationSets.question: How might a saved operational view explain its fixed definition without presenting that definition as removable filters?
explorationSets.context: The existing view mixed the fixed saved-view definition with user-controlled filtering. Alternative structural directions were needed before committing to a new header/filter model.
axesOfDifference: Where the fixed view definition is explained.
How prominently the operational task is expressed.
How user-controlled narrowing is separated from the fixed definition.
constraints: Preserve the production message table and its row behaviour.
Use one stable name for the view.
Do not turn fixed definition terms into removable chips.
evaluationCriteria: Users can distinguish the fixed view definition from filters they control.
The operational task is immediately legible.
The solution does not require redesigning the underlying table.

alternatives.name: Option A · Definition outside
alternatives.intendedDifference: Move the fixed saved-view definition outside the filter model while keeping the rest of the toolbar comparatively conventional.

alternatives.name: Option B · Task-first toolbar
alternatives.intendedDifference: Make the operational task and user-controlled narrowing the dominant toolbar model, with the fixed definition explained separately.

testingNotes: Both directions clarified that the fixed definition was not removable.
The task-first direction better expressed the operational job without redesigning the table.
explorationSets.selectionRationale: The task-first direction made the purpose of the view clearest while preserving the trusted table and the distinction between fixed scope and user-controlled narrowing.

workingMode.requestedAmendment: No active amendment. Preserve v2 as the current accepted revision until a new design question or requested change is identified.
mustRemainUnchanged: The production message table and row behaviour.
The distinction between the fixed view definition and user-controlled filters.
acceptanceChecks: Any future candidate starts from v2 rather than from one of the old exploration alternatives.
Exploration alternatives remain attached to v1 as design history, not treated as current versions.

decisionLog.decision: Keep one stable view name across navigation, breadcrumb and page context.
decisionLog.rationale: Competing names made the object model harder to understand.

decisionLog.decision: Treat the saved-view definition as explanatory copy, not removable filter chips.
decisionLog.rationale: The definition describes the fixed scope of the view; user filters only narrow within it.

decisionLog.decision: Promote the task-first exploration into accepted revision v2.
decisionLog.rationale: It best expressed the operational job while preserving the existing message table.

decisionLog.decision: Preserve the existing message table behaviour.
decisionLog.rationale: The design question concerns the header/filter model, not a redesign of the underlying table.

decisionLog.decision: Do not promote the definition-outside exploration.
decisionLog.rationale: It clarified the fixed definition, but it did not express the operational task as strongly as the task-first direction.

context.problem: A saved operational view has a fixed definition, but the existing filter presentation can make that definition look removable or user-controlled.
context.intendedOutcome: Explain the fixed scope of the view while letting users confidently narrow results with their own filters.
users: Security operations users reviewing messages requiring remediation
context.workflow: Users open a stable Needs Remediation view, understand its fixed definition, then narrow within it using operational filters while preserving the existing table workflow.
context.currentDirection: Accepted revision v2 uses a task-first header and toolbar that states the job clearly, separates the fixed view definition from user-controlled narrowing and leaves the production table intact.
constraints: Preserve the trusted production table and row behaviour.
Use one stable name for the view.
Do not represent fixed definition terms as removable filter chips.
acceptedDecisions: Use the task-first toolbar as the current accepted direction.
Keep the fixed definition separate from user-controlled filters.
Treat the earlier alternatives as one exploration set attached to v1.
openQuestions: How much explanatory copy is needed before the fixed definition becomes visually heavy?
Which parts of the task-first model should become reusable product patterns?
